description: The code-only release that heals a pool whose runtime runs but refuses: exactly the code policy, plus a stated root restart. The new controller code stops that runtime gracefully and its recovery starts a new one, so acceptance waits for the new boot and then requires every request on it. A failure is not rolled back: the code before it could not restart the pool. Its database rows are exactly what a release from main applies today: the named commands, and the two connections only while their origin waits on those commands. The last three commands exist on test stages only, so stage-heal runs this same policy. The root's row may plan only as the update the old release layer left behind: its recorded image hash, nothing else. The provider then reads the application, finds it equal and sends nothing; if it ever differs, the wire guard stops the apply at the root's modify request, after the pool Worker's upload. The root's row may also plan as an update whose only other difference is its attachment, while the pool Worker updates: one of the Worker's settings waits on a row that runs in the same plan (the pool database command's outcome), so the planner cannot know the attachment until the Worker applies. That is a standing shape on every release that changes what the pool database command is keyed on. It is admitted only when the namespace it resolves to is already recorded, equal on both rows, and the pool Worker still hosts the class; the apply then reads the application and sends nothing.

values.name: EXECUTOR_TELEMETRY
values.why: A secret: the telemetry settings with their credential, and beside them the release's build version, which differs on every release. Only that one field may differ. A changed endpoint or credential in it refuses, like any other secret.

codeOnly.why: The release ships main as a whole. Holding the bulk-import store's Worker at older code while the pool Worker and the history schema move is version skew, so its code moves with the rest. Only its code. The rule: every property, setting and binding of this Worker is the same in the plan as in State, in the last finished generation and, after an interrupted apply, in the unfinished one as well, whatever the plan calls the row; either may be what is live. Three exceptions. Its entry file may sit under another checkout's directory. A setting named under values may differ in its named fields. A setting named under references may be any copy of its resource, or the resource itself while that updates, provided its one binding holds one wire entry, named after the setting and as State has it; that binding alone may differ in the copy of a database connection's origin that local development reads, which no upload carries. Anything else refuses here. Its upload must also carry the serving version's bindings and no migration (wire.fixedBindings), so its Durable Object classes and their stored jobs stay as they are. The Worker has three more bindings that are not settings of its own: the two source stores and the vault bucket. They are named in neither list, so a refusal that names one of them, or any other binding, is a real change to what this Worker is attached to. It is not a healing release's to carry: ship it in a normal release.

rootRestart.why: A stated bound, not derived from the pool's constants: acceptable only because no production release runs before the release-bounds PR replaces it with one derived from the pool's named constants (worst case about 555 s plus destroy plus one membership pass when in-flight streams are counted). Until then it is the rehearsal's bound only.
